newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Asian Banking Corp.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Asian Banking Corp.

text.p: Asian debt markets got off to a slow start on Monday.

South Korea's Asian Banking Corp set a US$100 million floating rate note issue via lead manager Deutsche Morgan Grenfell. The notes mature in five years but can be put or called on the third and fourth anniversaries.
The notes pay a coupon of 65 basis points over the six-month London Interbank Offered Rates and, with fees, an all-in return of 75 basis points for all levels.
In October, the bank set a five-year, three-year put floating rate certificate of deposit issue that paid a coupon of 55 basis points and an all-in return of 70 basis points.
Indonesia's Central Sumahi Motor launched a two billion yen floating rate note through AB Capital Markets, LTCB Asia and Societe Generale Asia.
The five-year issue has annual puts and calls. It pays a coupon of 175 basis points over six-month Yen LIBOR and an all-in return of 200 basis points.
The notes are guaranteed by PT Indomobil Investment Corp.
Bankers said the deal is likely to be attractive because of its high coupon. The guarantor is the the second-largest automaker in Indonesia after PT Astra, one banker noted.
In other news, joint lead manager Lehman Brothers said it expects Thailand's US$600 million Yankee bond to tighten 10-15 basis points in the secondary market by year-end.
The 10-year bond was launched earlier this month to yield 90 basis points over comparable Treasuries.
"The spread has tightened to 86-88 basis points and should continue to tighten over time," Stephen Taran, credit research manager at Lehman, said in Bangkok on Monday.

"This will happen on the back of growing evidence that the government short-term adjustment policies are working, the continuing consolidation in the financial sector and increased recognition that the government's strategy to address structural problems is credible, he said.
